newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile pension funds' 1996 return on assets 3.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Chile pension funds' 1996 return on assets 3.5 pct.

text.p: Chilean pensions posted a 3.5 percent return on their assets in 1996, despite a negative return of 1.5 percent in December, Pension Funds Superintendent Julio Bustamanate reported Thursday.
The figures reflected in part the stagnant performance last year of the Santiago stock exchange, where the pension funds have major investments.
Bustamante said the overall gain in 1996 was due largely to the funds' investments in fixed-income markets, which in Chile tend to rise as stocks fall.
In stocks alone, pension funds' return on assets was a negative 3.01 percent last year, he said.
The figures, released monthly by the superintendent's office, measure the return on assets by Chile's whole private pension funds system.
With about $25 billion in its coffers, the system is a huge player in financial markets, and its rate of return on assets is watched as a kind of barometer of profitability in financial markets.
